long_biography.plain_text:
At fifteen, Igor Olenicoff began stocking shelves in a builders' hardware shop after his family reached the United States as refugees. He kept the job through school and university, learning about materials and construction. That experience helped turn his attention towards property, while borrowing and holding assets for decades became central to his investment approach.

He has also served as president of the Andrei Olenicoff Memorial Foundation, established in memory of his son. Its work includes support for people with visual impairments and research into eye disease. Beneficiaries have included Guide Dogs for the Blind, the Braille Institute and local community organisations.
